title: How a Water Tower Works in 60 Seconds 💧🗼 #shorts
description:
A water tower is a giant tank lifted high so gravity can push water to every tap in town. Pumps fill it at night when demand is low, and every foot of height adds about 0.43 psi of pressure. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#watertower #engineering #howitworks

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: Every *foot* a water tower rises adds about *0.43 psi* of pressure at your tap.

steps.label: Fill
steps.text: At night, when demand is low, *pumps* push clean water up a pipe into the *tank*.

steps.label: Gravity
steps.text: By day, *gravity* pulls that water back down through the mains to every home.

steps.label: Height
steps.text: A tank about *100 feet* up gives roughly *43 psi*, enough for a strong shower.

steps.label: Rush hour
steps.text: In the morning rush, the tower covers the *peak*, so the pumps can stay *smaller*.

steps.label: Backup
steps.text: It also stores water for *firefighters* and keeps taps running in a *power outage*.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Pump up, *gravity* down. Follow Inside 60 for more.
